findings.title: Passkeys conditional UI now disabled for regular (non-reauth) login
findings.body:
`isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(UserModel user)` returns true only when `user != null`. Previously `fillContextForm` was called when the user was *not* yet identified (the normal first login).

With this change, in `authenticate()` (line 115) and in `challenge(context, error, field)` (line 137), the passkey challenge and conditional-UI attributes are only set during re-authentication. On a fresh login (`context.getUser() == null`) the webauthn form and `ENABLE_WEBAUTHN_CONDITIONAL_UI` are never rendered, so passkey login on the initial screen breaks. Error re-renders after a bad username/password also lose the passkeys UI.

The existing tests that expect `//form[@id='webauth']` on the first login page would fail. The condition should not require a user (e.g. `webauthnAuth != null && webauthnAuth.isPasskeysEnabled()`), or should accept both cases.

findings.title: Call to non-existent no-arg isConditionalPasskeysEnabled() – compilation error
findings.body:
`UsernameForm.authenticate` calls `isConditionalPasskeysEnabled()` with no arguments. The superclass `UsernamePasswordForm` only declares `isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(UserModel user)`, and no no-arg overload exists, so this class does not compile.

It likely should be `isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(context.getUser())`, or simply `webauthnAuth != null && webauthnAuth.isPasskeysEnabled()`. Whichever form is chosen should be consistent with the fix to the helper's semantics.

findings.title: Overriding method lacks @Override
findings.body: `shouldShowWebAuthnAuthenticators` overrides `WebAuthnAuthenticator.shouldShowWebAuthnAuthenticators` but is not annotated with `@Override`. If the parent signature is renamed or changed, this would silently become a new method, and authenticators would again be listed in conditional UI. Add `@Override`.
